sections.Kurzabstract: The questionnaire serves to measure aspects of "Schmerzakzeptanz", defined as "efforts to maintain one's own level of functioning despite existing limitations as well as the tendency not to want to avoid pain at any price" (Nilges et al., 2007, S. 60). Persons with high pain acceptance accordingly focus their attention less on the pain and its elimination than on possibilities of actively participating in private, social and occupational life despite certain pain-related impairments. The CPAQ-D contains 20 statements relating to dealing with and appraising chronic pain. They are combined into two subscales: (1) Activity readiness (AB; k = 10) and (2) Pain readiness (SB; k = 8). Reliability: Cronbach's alpha is alpha = .84-.87. Validity: Both CPAQ-D subscales and the total scale correlated moderately to highly negatively with indicators of psychological burden (e.g. ADS-L, HADS-D, CSQ, PDI, SES). In contrast, no or only weak associations were found with further pain measures, e.g. the chronification stage according to the Mainzer Stadienkonzept chronischer Schmerzen, sensory pain intensity, pain duration to date in years and further indicators of pain intensity, as well as experimentally assessed differences in thermal pain threshold. Furthermore, no association between current pain intensity and pain acceptance could be demonstrated (r = .16).
sections.Diagnostische Zielsetzung: The questionnaire serves to measure aspects of "Schmerzakzeptanz", defined as "efforts to maintain one's own level of functioning despite existing limitations as well as the tendency not to want to avoid pain at any price" (Nilges et al., 2007, S. 60). Persons with high pain acceptance accordingly focus their attention less on the pain and its elimination than on possibilities of actively participating in private, social and occupational life despite certain pain-related impairments. The instrument can be used in research and clinical practice with patients with chronic pain problems in order to obtain indications of dysfunctional pain-related cognitions and coping styles.
sections.Aufbau:
The CPAQ-D contains 20 statements relating to dealing with and appraising chronic pain, which patients are to rate on a seven-point frequency scale from 0 = "nie" to 6 = "immer". 18 of the 20 items are combined into two subscales by adding the raw scores:
(1) Activity readiness (AB; k = 10: items 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 15, 19; range of values 0-60): continuing daily tasks and leisure activities in the usual way even when pain is present (example item: "Ich komme mit meinen täglichen Aufgaben klar, egal wie stark meine Schmerzen sind").
(2) Pain readiness (SB; k = 8: items 4, 7, 11, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18; range of values: 0-48): recognition that attempts to avoid or control pain are often ineffective and that an orientation towards other, less impaired areas of life and attainable goals makes sense (all items are negatively worded and must therefore be reversed; example item: "Bevor ich irgendwelche ernsthaften Pläne schmieden kann, muss ich zunächst etwas Kontrolle über meine Schmerzen gewinnen").
Across the 18 items, a total score for pain acceptance can be formed, with a range of values between 0 and 108.
Two items are not included in either of the two scales but should be left in the questionnaire in order to ensure, in a research context, the comparability of the CPAQ-D with international versions of the instrument.
sections.Grundlagen und Konstruktion:
Numerous studies show that the course of chronic pain problems is determined only to a very limited extent by the effectiveness of medical treatment measures, but substantially by pain-related cognitions and coping styles (for an overview see e.g. Turk & Okifuji, 2002). Although an active role of patients is an important prerequisite for successful pain coping, action-oriented, uncompromisingly combative or recovery-oriented forms of coping reach their limits in chronified pain problems: The expectation of achieving extensive or even complete freedom from pain and pain-related impairments through ever new therapies and medication trials is an unrealistic goal for many patients. For these patients, "Schmerzakzeptanz" - in the sense of a modification of expectations, goals and appraisals - can be regarded as a more functional form of coping (Nilges et al., 2007): The aim is to develop the willingness to maintain activities despite existing pain within the limits of what is possible, to accept permanent physical limitations and social changes, and to set new goals that are not threatened by the pain. With the CPAQ-D, the constructs "Aktivitätsbereitschaft" and "Schmerzbereitschaft" are operationalized as two facets of pain acceptance. The questionnaire is based on cognitive coping-theoretical concepts. It draws in particular on the two-process model by Brandtstädter (1992). Pain acceptance can accordingly be interpreted as a form of dealing with chronic pain that is to be assigned to the accommodative, flexible coping mode: Discrepancies between the real and the desired situation are reduced by accepting or reinterpreting the real situation and by replacing goals that have become unattainable with new, more realistic ones. High dispositional flexibility proved, among other things, to be a protective factor that buffered effects of pain intensity on depression (Schmitz, Saile & Nilges, 1996).
The German version CPAQ-D is based on the revised version of the English-language original instrument by McCracken (1998; McCracken, Vowles & Eccleston, 2004) and was developed in cooperation with the first author of the English version. The instrument was first translated into German, back-translated into English by an independent person and compared with the original by the authors. Content corrections were subsequently made for two items. The psychometric examination of the corrected German version was guided by classical test theory. The construction sample comprised N = 150 inpatients of the DRK-Schmerzzentrum Mainz and was composed of two subsamples (n = 100 and n = 50). A principal component analysis computed to determine the factorial structure, followed by oblique rotation according to the direct oblimin criterion, yielded a two-factor solution (explained variance: 43.2%). The two factors could be interpreted, as expected, as "Aktivitätsbereitschaft" and "Schmerzbereitschaft", and 18 of the 20 items showed loading patterns corresponding to the theoretical expectations, so that the two scales of the CPAQ-D could be constructed on this basis. The part-whole-corrected item discrimination values, after elimination of the two unsuitable items, were consistently in the satisfactory to good range, with values of .39 to .67 ("Aktivitätsbereitschaft") and .44 to .72 ("Schmerzbereitschaft") (Nilges et al., 2007).
sections.Empirische Prüfung und Gütekriterien:
Reliability: The internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) of the two subscales is alpha = .84 in each case, and that of the total scale consisting of 18 items is alpha = .87 (Nilges et al., 2007).
Validity: Both CPAQ-D subscales and the total scale correlated moderately to highly negatively with indicators of psychological burden in the construction sample (N = 150) (Nilges et al., 2007, S. 64). For the CPAQ-D total score, correlations of r = .64 with the Allgemeine Depressionsskala ADS-L (Hautzinger & Bailer, 1993), r = .49 with the subscale "Depression" and r = .54 with the subscale "Angst" of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale HADS-D (Herrmann, Buss & Snaith, 1995) as well as r = .45 with the subscale "Katastrophisierendes Coping" of the Coping Strategies Questionnaire CSQ (Rosenstiel & Keefe, 1983) were found. Moderate negative correlations were also found between the CPAQ-D and measures of pain-related impairment (r = .43 with the Pain Disability Index PDI; Dillmann, Nilges, Saile & Gerbershagen, 1994) as well as affective pain intensity (r = .45 with the corresponding subscale of the Schmerzempfindungsskala SES; Geissner, 1996). In contrast, no or only weak associations were found with further pain measures, e.g. the chronification stage according to the Mainzer Stadienkonzept chronischer Schmerzen (r = .01), sensory pain intensity (r = .17), pain duration to date in years (r = .01) and further indicators of pain intensity as well as - examined in a subgroup of n = 50 patients - experimentally assessed differences in thermal pain threshold. Furthermore, no association between current pain intensity and pain acceptance could be demonstrated (r = .16). Overall, there is thus no indication that the extent of current complaints influences the answering of the CPAQ-D questions, or that "Schmerzakzeptanz" represents a form of cognitive coping that is primarily determined by the severity of the pain itself.
Norms: Percentile norms (10th, 25th, 50th, 75th, 90th percentile) are available for the 18-item version (Nilges et al., 2007, S. 64). The values were obtained from the N = 150 participants of the German construction sample. These were inpatients of the DRK-Schmerzzentrum Mainz aged 19 to 77 years (M = 48.3 years, SD = 11.5 years; 36.7 % men, 63.3 % women) with an average pain duration of almost 10 years.
sections.Durchführung/Altersbereiche: The Chronic Pain Acceptance Questionnaire (CPAQ-D; Nilges, Köster & Schmidt, 2007) was developed and validated in samples of adults.
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungszeit: Completing the questionnaire takes about 5 to 10 minutes.
sections.Bewertung: The CPAQ-D is an economical German-language instrument for measuring the construct "Schmerzakzeptanz" which, according to a first study, shows very favourable psychometric properties and has also proven itself internationally. It would be desirable to supplement the findings with further studies examining the scale structure, the predictive validity of the instrument and the modifiability of cognitions, e.g. through cognitive or cognitive-behavioural pain therapy intervention programmes.

Study.Instructions: Im folgenden finden Sie eine Liste mit Feststellungen zu chronischen Schmerzen. Bitte lesen Sie sich jeden Satz durch und wählen Sie aus den sieben möglichen Antworten diejenige aus, die am besten angibt, in welchem Ausmaß Sie der Aussage zustimmen. Bitte kreuzen Sie bei jeder Feststellung die für Sie zutreffende Zahl an. Ich stimme zu….

CPAQD01.Description: Ich komme mit meinen täglichen Aufgaben klar, egal wie stark meine Schmerzen sind.

CPAQD02.Description: Mein Leben verläuft gut, auch wenn ich an chronischen Schmerzen leide.

CPAQD03.Description: Es ist in Ordnung Schmerzen zu erleben.

CPAQD04.Description: Ich würde liebend gerne Dinge, die mir wichtig sind, opfern, wenn ich dann meine Schmerzen besser kontrollieren könnte.

CPAQD05.Description: Es ist für mich nicht notwendig, meine Schmerzen im Griff zu haben, um mein Leben gut bewältigen zu können.

CPAQD06.Description: Auch wenn es Veränderungen gegeben hat, führe ich trotz meiner chronischen Schmerzen ein normales Leben.

CPAQD07.Description: Ich muss mich darauf konzentrieren, meine Schmerzen los zu werden.

CPAQD08.Description: Es gibt viele Aktivitäten, denen ich nachgehe, wenn ich Schmerzen habe.

CPAQD09.Description: Obwohl ich an chronischen Schmerzen leide, führe ich ein erfülltes Leben.

CPAQD10.Description: Meine anderen Lebensziele sind mir alle wichtiger als die Kontrolle meiner Schmerzen.

CPAQD11.Description: Bevor ich wichtige Veränderungen in meinem Leben vornehmen kann, müssen sich meine Gedanken und Gefühle dem Schmerz gegenüber verändern.

CPAQD12.Description: Trotz der Schmerzen verfolge ich inzwischen einen bestimmten Lebensweg.

CPAQD13.Description: Immer, wenn ich etwas mache, hat die Kontrolle meiner Schmerzen erste Priorität.

CPAQD14.Description: Bevor ich irgendwelche ernsthaften Pläne schmieden kann, muss ich zunächst etwas Kontrolle über meine Schmerzen gewinnen.

CPAQD15.Description: Auch wenn meine Schmerzen stärker werden, kann ich meinen Verpflichtungen immer noch nachkommen.

CPAQD16.Description: Ich würde mein Leben besser im Griff haben, wenn ich meine negativen Gedanken in Bezug auf die Schmerzen besser kontrollieren könnte.

CPAQD17.Description: Ich vermeide es, mich in Situationen zu bringen, in denen meine Schmerzen schlimmer werden könnten.

CPAQD18.Description: Meine Sorgen und Ängste darüber, was der Schmerz mit mir machen könnte, stimmen.

CPAQD19.Description: Es ist eine Erleichterung zu erkennen, dass ich an meinen Schmerzen nichts verändern muss, um mit meinem Leben klar zu kommen.

CPAQD20.Description: Wenn ich Schmerzen habe, kostet es mich große Überwindung etwas zu machen.
